spec.title: vibe tree — the interactive spec-tree browser

p.purpose: **Purpose.** `vibe tree` (PROP-036) is an interactive terminal UI: it renders the resolved package tree, lets a human navigate/fold it, opens a detail modal, and cycles ordering + display modes. The automated suite proves the *model* (the engine + `--json` validate against the schema, and the flat renderer has unit tests), but it cannot drive a real terminal and confirm that the tree *renders and reads right* — the box-drawing aligns, the selection highlights, the keys respond, the modal overlays cleanly, and colour works on this terminal. That is what a human proves here. `vibe tree` is **read-only** (it mutates nothing — no per-user state, no project files), so this test needs no state isolation; it runs against the vibevm repo itself, which is a rich real tree.

facts.PRE-TTY: A real interactive terminal (a tty) — this is the whole point; the TUI does not launch when stdout is piped or redirected.
facts.PRE-BINARY: The working-tree binary built from this repo: `cargo build -p vibe-cli` (invoke it as `./target/debug/vibe`, never a stale PATH `vibe`).
facts.PRE-REPO-ROOT: Run from the vibevm repo root (its `vibe.lock` + `vibevm/vibespecs/boot/{STATIC,INDEX}.md` are the tree under test). No network, no credentials.

section.title: Setup
section.fence: cargo build -p vibe-cli cd <vibevm repo root> # the project whose tree is rendered

p.setup-no-isolation: No scratch/state redirect is needed: `vibe tree` reads `vibe.lock`, the manifests, and the committed boot artifacts, and writes nothing.

section.title: Steps

facts.STEP-1-MACHINE-SURFACE: The machine surface still works (non-tty fallbacks).

p.EXP-1-MACHINE-SURFACE: **Expected.** `--json` prints an object opening `{"ok":true,"command":"tree",` with `"schema_version":1`. `--plain` prints a static ASCII tree: a header line (`project: …`), a `STATIC.md: … bytes / … lines` line, a `columns: load T=… C=… S=…` legend, then rows drawn with `│ ├ └` and a `load` column (`static`/`dynamic`/`none`) plus three checkbox columns. `redbook` shows `static` with `S = x`; `rust-ai-native` (the umbrella) shows `none`. Neither command clears the screen or waits for input.

p.EXP-2-LAUNCH-TUI: **Expected.** The terminal switches to a full-screen view. A **status line** reads `ordering: topological mode: all STATIC.md: <N> bytes / <N> lines packages: <N>`. A **footer** shows the keymap hint (`F1 search · F2 sort · F3 mode · F4 settings · F6 copy · ↑↓ move · ←→ pan · Space fold · Enter details · Esc quit`). The tree fills the body; the first row is highlighted (reverse/coloured).

p.EXP-3-NAVIGATE: **Expected.** `↓`/`↑` move the highlight one row and the view scrolls to keep the selection on screen when you reach the bottom/top. `←`/`→` pan the name column horizontally (deep/long ids that ran off the right edge come into view; the `load`/checkbox columns stay fixed).

p.EXP-4-FOLD: **Expected.** With a node that has children selected, `Space` collapses its subtree and the node's indicator flips to `+`; `Space` again expands it back to `-`. `F` folds the whole tree to its roots (all `+`); `F` again unfolds everything. A package reached twice (a diamond) shows once expanded and once as a `(*)` leaf.

section.fence: (press Enter on a selected package row)

p.EXP-5-DETAIL-MODAL: **Expected.** A bordered popup overlays the tree (the cells beneath are cleared, not bled through) showing the package's detail **vertically**: name, group, version, kind, load type, transitive (+ why), condition, in-STATIC.md, source, content hash, dependencies, boot file. `Esc` closes it and returns to the tree at the same selection. While the modal is open, other keys are swallowed (do not move the tree).

p.EXP-6-ORDERING: **Expected.** The F2 sort menu opens. Choosing `alphabetical` closes it, the status line's `ordering:` flips to `alphabetical`, and the siblings re-sort by `group/name` (the tree structure is preserved — a parent still precedes its children). F2 again and `topological` returns.

section.fence: (press F3, choose each mode in turn)

p.EXP-7-MODES: **Expected.** The F3 mode menu opens. **sub-tables**: a flat list under bold subheaders `static dependencies`, `dynamic dependencies`, `no-boot` (`mode: sub-tables` in the status line). **tabs**: a tab bar `Static | Dynamic | No-boot` with one group's flat list below (`mode: tabs`). **all**: back to the tree. In every mode the `load`/T/C/S columns stay meaningful.

section.fence: (in tabs mode: press Shift+→, then Shift+←)

p.EXP-8-SWAP-TABS: **Expected.** In tabs mode `Shift+→` advances to the next tab (wrapping) and `Shift+←` goes back; the shown flat list changes to the active group. The static/dynamic priority is a setting, reachable from the F4 settings menu — the pre-Spec-2 bare `t` / `Tab` / `[` / `]` bindings do not ship.

p.EXP-9-QUIT: **Expected.** A `Really quit?` confirm dialog appears; confirming exits the TUI, the alternate screen is torn down, and the normal terminal (with your scrollback intact) is restored — no leftover raw-mode, no garbled prompt, exit code 0.

p.teardown-none: None — `vibe tree` wrote nothing. (If a crash ever leaves the terminal in raw mode, `reset` restores it.)

section.title: What to file if it fails

facts.FAIL-STEP-NUMBER: The failing step number; what you saw beside its **Expected**.
facts.FAIL-SCREENSHOT: A screenshot or a copy of the mis-rendered frame (the exact glyphs/colours).
facts.FAIL-MODEL-OUTPUT: `./target/debug/vibe tree --json` output (the model the TUI renders) and `./target/debug/vibe tree --plain` (the same tree, copy-pasteable).
